record.name: Timor-Leste
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. Timor-Leste completed a UNESCO AI readiness assessment with the Ministry of Transport and Communications, and the main digital strategy (Timor Digital 2032) does not explicitly address AI.

related_bodies.name: Ministry of Transport and Communications
related_bodies.role: It is a partner in the UNESCO AI readiness assessment. This was reported by Catalpa International.

related_bodies.name: TIC Timor
related_bodies.role: It is a partner in the readiness assessment. It is a government ICT agency.

The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Only the UNESCO catalogue record, not the underlying report, was read; Catalpa and UNESCO also describe the same co-produced readiness project. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.
check.governance_note: Delivery partner Catalpa International's firsthand account identifies the ministry, TIC Timor and UNESCO as the national AI-readiness assessment partners. This is process evidence; the full readiness report was not read.

record.notes: Cited foreign sources for the governance context: UNESCO; Catalpa International; ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute. The UNESCO AI readiness assessment report is catalogued in UNESDOC (2025, 96 pages); only its catalogue record was read, not the report. The delivery partner's project page is a firsthand account of its participation; the ISEAS paper is secondary analysis. English and Portuguese-term searches.
